limitations: The fixed pickup library is the peer 62-reference experimental library, not the production pickup library.
The on arm reuses hash-verified full replay outputs from the preceding experiment; one short on replay was freshly rerun and identical.
The off arm freshly replays all 8156.6 seconds of exactly the same decoded mono 24 kHz WAV inputs.
Success means accepted candidate-set output, not unique-item guessing. Hidden trader sound-family correctness is unverified.
Only explicit known operations and previously visually reviewed negatives are scored; no overall accuracy estimate.
No putdown branch activation in a recording means no decision change; it does not prove the auxiliary score always fails its raw threshold.
Synthetic timing of explicit reference controls proves loading/branch activation, not real-world recognition quality.
The CLI replay uses audio timestamps and does not simulate GUI scheduling, CPU-busy skipped scans or actual display latency.
Peer pickup groups and original putdown groups have different identifiers; this ablation is not an end-to-end GUI same-group confirmation test.
No conclusion that the auxiliary library can never help on other recordings, thresholds or reference libraries.
